dimensions.assessment: Affects all minors, parents, and commercial online platforms, social media networks, video game providers, and chatbot providers nationwide.
dimensions.evidence: To protect children and teens online, empower parents and strengthen families, and for other purposes.

dimensions.assessment: Major operational and compliance changes for technology companies, along with significant privacy and safety changes for minors and parents online.
dimensions.evidence: This bill requires specified online platforms to establish safeguards for minors.

dimensions.assessment: Establishes annual registration fees of at least $22,500 for covered data brokers and directs multiple federal agencies to conduct studies and reports.
dimensions.evidence: The Commission may charge a covered data broker an annual registration fee of at least $22,500

dimensions.assessment: Creates sweeping new regulatory frameworks, mandates platform design changes, requires third-party audits, expands COPPA to teens, and establishes enforcement powers for the FTC and state attorneys general.
dimensions.evidence: A violation of this Act shall be treated as a violation of a regulation under section 18(a)(1)(B) of the Federal Trade Commission Act

dimensions.assessment: Permanent statutory requirements with ongoing reporting, auditing, and compliance obligations spanning the national digital economy.

summary: The KIDS Act establishes various online safety, privacy, and parental control requirements for technology platforms, video games, artificial intelligence chatbots, and data brokers concerning minors. It mandates age verification on websites containing sexual material, creates default safety settings and parental tools on social media and video game platforms, updates the Children's Online Privacy Protection Act (COPPA 2.0), requires data broker registration, and provides for enforcement by the Federal Trade Commission and state attorneys general.

affected_groups.effect: Will receive enhanced online safeguards, default protective settings on social media and video games, restrictions on targeted advertising and ephemeral messaging, and clear disclosures from AI chatbots.
affected_groups.group: Minors (Individuals under 17 or 18 depending on the section)

affected_groups.effect: Granted new tools to view account settings, manage privacy controls, restrict purchases, monitor time spent, and receive notifications regarding direct messaging requests for minor children.
Must implement new technical safeguards, default settings, independent audits, reporting mechanisms, and age-verification or parental-control capabilities.
affected_groups.group: Online Platforms and Social Media Providers

affected_groups.effect: Must display mandatory AI and crisis hotline disclosures to minors, prohibit claims of being a licensed professional, and implement policies for 3-hour break reminders.
Required to register annually with the Federal Trade Commission, pay registration fees, and provide searchable public registry information regarding their data practices concerning minors.

key_provisions: Requires publicly available online platforms where more than one-third of content is sexual material harmful to minors to adopt commercially available technology verification measures to identify minors and prevent them from accessing such material.

Mandates that social media platforms implement default settings for minors that limit compulsive usage features and communication from other users, prohibit ephemeral messaging features for minors, and provide parental management tools.
Requires online video game providers to offer parental communication and purchase restriction tools that are set to the most protective level by default for minor users.

Requires AI chatbot providers to clearly disclose to minor users that the system is artificial intelligence, provide suicide and crisis intervention hotline information upon prompting, and advise breaks after three hours of continuous use.
Updates COPPA to expand personal information protections and extend rules to cover teens under age 18, including banning individual-specific advertising to children and teens.
Requires covered data brokers that sell or transfer personal data of minors to register annually with the Federal Trade Commission and pay a fee.
missing_information: Specific funding levels or appropriations for federal agencies to carry out the required studies, reports, and educational campaigns.

Specific civil penalty amounts for violations of the act, beyond stating that violations are treated as violations of rules regarding unfair or deceptive acts or practices under the Federal Trade Commission Act.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The KIDS Act establishes various online safety, privacy, and parental control requirements for technology platforms, video games, artificial intelligence chatbots, and data brokers concerning minors. It mandates age verification on websites containing sexual material, creates default safety settings and parental tools on social media and video game platforms, updates the Children's Online Privacy Protection Act (COPPA 2.0), requires data broker registration, and provides for enforcement by the Federal Trade Commission and state attorneys general.
summary_detail.significance: The bill establishes comprehensive federal regulations regarding minors' internet safety, privacy, and digital interactions. It impacts major sectors of the digital economy—including social media companies, video game providers, AI developers, and data brokers—while expanding federal and state enforcement powers through the FTC and state attorneys general.
